HTTP API ​

Every route the orchestrator serves lives under /api on one Express app . The same HTTP server also carries the WebSocket stream, so the API origin and the live-data origin are always identical.

Base URL ​

The API is same-origin with the app: every path below is relative to your workspace URL, as https://<your-workspace-host>/api/…. Because the SPA, the API and the WebSocket share an origin, browser calls need no CORS handling and no second host.

Response envelope ​

Almost every JSON route returns an ok flag; failures carry a human error string. File-serving routes return bytes with a MIME type instead.

json
{ "ok": true,  "run": { "id": "…" } }
{ "ok": false, "error": "No such run" }

The terminal error handler maps body-parser failures to 400 Invalid JSON body and 413 Payload too large, and anything unexpected to 500 Internal error — a stack is never returned.

Authentication ​

Every request is authenticated. The stack mounts in this exact order:

LayerWhat it does
/api/webhooksPublic ingress, mounted first with its own limiter
shared limiter600 requests/min per IP across /api
/api/healthAlways reachable, even while Mongo is down
/api/bootstrapPublic; the handshake the client boots from
csrfOriginCheckOrigin check for the cookie-authenticated API
/api/authPublic login/signup/reset/OAuth surface
requireSession401 without a valid saidi_session cookie
org-less routes/api/orgs, /api/invites, /api/admin
orgContextReads the X-Saidi-Org header, verifies membership, enters the tenant scope. Missing header → 400
permission gatesPer-router write gates (below)
org-scoped routersRuns, chats, memory, crons, reflexes, …

Credential endpoints get a second, much stricter limiter in front of the shared bucket: 10 requests/min keyed on IP + the submitted email, covering /api/auth/login, /api/auth/forgot-password, /api/auth/reset-password, /api/auth/verify-email, and the OAuth callback.

Permission gates ​

PrefixGate
/api/settings, /api/secrets, /api/telegram, /api/import, /api/onboardingPlatform superadmin only (reads included)
/api/providersReads open; writes require superadmin
/api/cronsWrites require crons.manage
/api/reflexesWrites require reflexes.manage
/api/memoryWrites require memory.manage
/api/admin/*Platform superadmin

Runs, run files, run git views, and run assets share one ACL (http/routes/run-acl.ts): you may view a run you own, a run shared to you, or any run if you hold runs.viewAll; you may steer a run you own or any run if you hold runs.steerAll. A refused request returns 403 with "You do not have access to this run." Chats apply the same shape with chats.viewAll.

MongoDB is the sole structured store. While it is disconnected, every /api route except /api/health returns 503 { ok: false, error: "MongoDB unavailable" }.

Health & bootstrap ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/health{ ok, mongo }. 200 when Mongo is connected, 503 otherwise
GET/api/bootstrapLocal: { ok, mode: 'local' }. Cloud: { ok, mode: 'cloud', providers, user?, orgs? }. A session that cannot be resolved returns 503 (retry) rather than pretending you are logged out

State ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/stateThe full dashboard snapshot — rosters, memory, runs, chats. Scoped to the requesting member in cloud mode; fails closed with 401 if the tenant locals are incomplete
POST/api/state/reloadRe-hydrates the in-memory stores from MongoDB, then returns the fresh snapshot. The only runtime path that re-reads Mongo; it also nudges other dashboards to re-pull

Runs ​

See The Run Object for the shape of what these return.

MethodPathPurpose
GET/api/runs{ ok, runs } — summaries, filtered to what you may view
GET/api/runs/search?q=Full-text search over title/brief/thread → { id, snippet }[]
POST/api/runsCreate and start a run
GET/api/runs/:idOne run, thread included
PATCH/api/runs/:id/configRun-wide execution overrides
PATCH/api/runs/:id/agent-configOne actor's overrides
POST/api/runs/:id/rename{ title }, trimmed to 140 chars
PUT/api/runs/:id/share{ userIds: string[] } — replaces the viewer list
POST/api/runs/:id/message{ text, attachments? } — send into the thread
POST/api/runs/:id/attach-assets{ files?, includeAlreadyAttached?, note? }
POST/api/runs/:id/upload?name=Raw bytes, one file, 25 MB cap → { ok, file }
POST/api/runs/:id/control{ action }
POST/api/runs/:id/rewind{ eventId, text } — edit and resend your last message
POST/api/runs/:id/approval{ approve: boolean, note? }
POST/api/runs/:id/plan-approval{ approve: boolean, note? } — sign off on the plan itself
DELETE/api/runs/:idDeletes the record and its assets; ?files=0 keeps the on-disk folder

POST /api/runs body:

FieldTypeMeaning
briefstringRequired. Empty → 400
project?stringMust resolve against the registry (case-insensitive) or 404
effort?'low' | 'medium' | 'high'Omitted/invalid falls back to the Settings default
provider? / model?stringRun-wide overrides
executionMode?'guided' | 'autonomous'Anything else keeps the Settings default
playbookId?stringExplicit playbook wins; otherwise a saved plan for this exact brief is reused

A run that cannot start because of the credits hard stop or a cloud governance gate (budget, concurrency, suspension) returns 402 with the reason.

control accepts pause, resume, stop (halts the current turn, run stays open), done, cancel, reopen. Anything else is a 400.

The two PATCH config routes take provider, model, and effort — a string sets the value, '' clears it back to inherit, and an omitted key is left alone. agent-config additionally requires actor ('PRIME', a project, or an agent name). Both apply to future turns only, never retroactively.

Approval returns 202 when the decision was claimed (it queues behind a still-finishing turn) and 404 when nothing was pending.

Code view ​

Every git route verifies the run actually participates in the named project, so a viewable run id can never be used to read an unrelated org repo.

MethodPathQueryReturns
GET/api/runs/:id/git—Per-project snapshot: branches, commits, files, PR
GET/api/runs/:id/git/compareproject, base, headChanged-file list between two refs
GET/api/runs/:id/git/worktreeprojectUncommitted worktree changes
GET/api/runs/:id/git/fileproject, file, base, head, mode?One file's source
GET/api/runs/:id/git/diffproject, file, base, head, mode?One file's unified diff
POST/api/runs/:id/git/checkoutbody { project, branch }Switch the run's working branch
POST/api/runs/:id/publishbody { project, branch? }Push the branch and open a PR

mode=worktree makes base and head optional; otherwise both are required.

Run files ​

The on-disk folder of one run (assets/, work/<agent>/, and the run.json record). Paths are resolved and realpath-guarded inside the run directory, so neither .. nor a symlink can escape. run.json is protected from both delete routes.

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/runs/:id/files?path=Directory listing with recursive sizes, or capped file content. Caps: 500 entries, 256 KB of returned text, 8 MB per file. Binary files report binary: true
GET/api/runs/:id/fs?path=Raw bytes, MIME-typed — inline image view and downloads
DELETE/api/runs/:id/files?path=Delete one file or directory
DELETE/api/runs/:id/files/allClear everything except run.json

Playbooks ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/playbooksSaved plans available for replay
POST/api/runs/:id/playbook{ name? } — refuses an unfinished run
DELETE/api/playbooks/:idRemove a saved playbook

Chats ​

Metadata and history only. Sending messages and streaming replies is the WebSocket's job. A chat's transcript is not stored on the chat record — it lives in the activity stream tagged with the chat id.

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/chatsList (session id stripped)
POST/api/chats{ title? } → the new chat
GET/api/chats/:id{ ok, chat, recent } — up to 200 transcript rows, newest first, read durably from Mongo
PATCH/api/chats/:id{ title } — owner or chats.viewAll
PUT/api/chats/:id/share{ userIds: string[] }
DELETE/api/chats/:idDeletes the chat and wipes its transcript

Memory ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/memory?file=<relpath>{ ok, file, content }. Bad path → 400, missing → 404
POST/api/memory{ file, content }, 1 MB limit, path-traversal guarded

Crons ​

Clock-triggered scheduled work. Create/update validation is shared with PRIME's tools (see Orchestrator Tools).

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/cronsList
POST/api/crons{ name, schedule, brief, project?, enabled? }
PATCH/api/crons/:idAny of the same fields
DELETE/api/crons/:id
POST/api/crons/:id/runFire now → { ok, runId }. 409 if the previous run is still live

Reflexes ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/reflexesList
POST/api/reflexesCreate
PATCH/api/reflexes/:idUpdate any field
DELETE/api/reflexes/:id
POST/api/reflexes/:id/test{ payload, type? } — fires the action directly. 409 if the sample payload doesn't satisfy the match tree
GET/api/reflexes/log{ events, fires } — 150 of each
GET/api/reflexes/pendingFires parked for approval
POST/api/reflexes/pending/:id/approve
POST/api/reflexes/pending/:id/deny

A manual test bypasses cooldown and approval and does not count toward maxFires, but it still writes to the console log.

Webhooks ​

The only internet-facing surface, mounted at /api/webhooks with its own 300/min limiter ahead of the shared bucket. The raw body is kept for signature verification.

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/webhooks/:sourceSubscribe handshake — echoes hub.challenge when hub.mode=subscribe and hub.verify_token matches. Otherwise 403
POST/api/webhooks/:sourceVerify → normalize → push onto the bus → { ok, id, type, source }

Built-in sources and their credentials:

SourceVerificationSecret
genericBearer token in Authorization or X-Webhook-TokenSAIDI_WEBHOOK_GENERIC_TOKEN
githubHMAC-SHA256, X-Hub-Signature-256, sha256= hexSAIDI_WEBHOOK_GITHUB_SECRET
stripeHMAC over ${t}.${body}, Stripe-Signature v1, ±300 s replay windowSAIDI_WEBHOOK_STRIPE_SECRET
whatsapp, instagram, messenger, metaHMAC-SHA256, X-Hub-Signature-256SAIDI_WEBHOOK_META_SECRET

Any other name falls through to the env-configured path — no code needed:

SAIDI_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_SCHEME    bearer | hmac | none   (default: bearer if a secret is set)
SAIDI_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_SECRET    shared token or HMAC secret
SAIDI_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_HEADER    signature header       (hmac; default x-signature)
SAIDI_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_PREFIX    signature prefix       (hmac; default "sha256=", "" for none)
SAIDI_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_ENCODING  hex | base64           (hmac; default hex)
SAIDI_WEBHOOK_<NAME>_VERIFY_TOKEN  token for the GET challenge

A source with no configured secret is rejected 401 unless it explicitly opts into SCHEME=none. The POST acks fast with 200 — matching and actions run asynchronously on the bus, so the provider never retries on a slow reflex.

Assets & uploads ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/run-asset?run=&file=Serve a file an agent produced inside a run. Gated by the run view ACL, sandboxed to that run's assets/ dir, streamed with Range support
GET/api/chat-asset?file=Serve a main-chat upload from the org's chat-uploads/ dir
POST/api/chat/upload?name=Raw bytes, 25 MB cap → { ok, file }. The stored name carries 16 random bytes so filenames cannot be enumerated

Settings ​

Superadmin-only in cloud mode. Files stay the source of truth, so every edit is git-diffable.

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/settings{ agents, projects, system }
PUT/api/settings/agents/:namePatch agents/<name>/AGENT.md: description, department, model, cwd, prompt, lead, profile, effort, permission (all | read-only | custom), tools[]. An empty prompt is refused
DELETE/api/settings/agents/:nameRemove the whole agent directory
DELETE/api/settings/agents/:name/skills/:slugRemove one skill
DELETE/api/settings/agents/:name/mcp/:serverRemove one MCP server
PUT/api/settings/projects/:name{ branch: 'new' | 'current' | null, approval: 'confirm' | 'auto' | null } — null removes the declaration so the project inherits the system default
PUT/api/settings/systemPatch config/settings.json (ownerName, primeModel, defaultBranchMode, defaultApproval, cronTickSeconds ≥ 5, and the rest of the system knobs)

Agent and project writes reload the live roster in-process and push a state_dirty nudge, so PRIME sees the change on its next turn without a restart.

Secrets ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/secretsMasked view — { set, hint } per credential, redacted Mongo URI. Raw secrets are never returned
PUT/api/secretsPatch: a non-empty string sets, null clears, empty/absent leaves unchanged

Managed fields: mongodbUri, anthropicApiKey, anthropicAuthToken, claudeCodeOauthToken, anthropicModel, anthropicBaseUrl, openaiApiKey, saidiGithubToken, webhookGenericToken, webhookGithubSecret, webhookStripeSecret, webhookMetaSecret, webhookMetaVerifyToken. Values are validated before they are persisted, then applied to process.env live where possible.

Providers ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/providers{ profiles, defaultId } with tokens masked
POST/api/providersCreate or update a custom profile — id, name, and per-effort tiers (low/medium/high, each its own model, baseUrl, authToken, priceIn, priceOut)
POST/api/providers/testLive probe of { model, baseUrl?, authToken?, profileId?, effort? }. Posts a 16-token ping to <baseUrl>/v1/messages with a 20 s timeout and reports status + latency
DELETE/api/providers/:idDelete a custom profile; the built-ins refuse

Marketplace ​

Four package kinds — agent, department, skill, mcp. Installing or removing each kind is gated by its own org permission (market.install.<kind>).

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/marketplace/config{ registryUrl, installed }
PUT/api/marketplace/config{ registryUrl } — superadmin
GET/api/marketplace/sourcesAvailable browse sources
PUT/api/marketplace/sources/skillsmp-key{ key } — superadmin
GET/api/marketplace/packages?q=&kind=&registryUrl=Catalog search. Only a superadmin may override registryUrl (the SSRF surface)
POST/api/marketplace/preview{ packageUrl } — validate and describe before installing
POST/api/marketplace/install{ packageUrl, overwrite?, targetAgent?, createAgent? }
POST/api/marketplace/update{ id } — reinstall at latest, reusing the recorded target
POST/api/marketplace/uninstall{ id } → { ok, removed }
GET/api/marketplace/versions?id= · /reviews?id=Proxied to the hosted API
POST/api/marketplace/reviews · /report{ id, rating, text } · { id, reason, version? }
POST/api/marketplace/auth/start · /auth/pollGitHub device flow; the device code and GitHub access token stay server-side
GET/api/marketplace/account · POST /signoutPublisher identity
POST/api/marketplace/publish · /unpublishPublish to the hosted API or a GitHub repo via gh

Import ​

Additive/merge only — import never deletes anything in the target.

MethodPathBody
POST/api/import/agents/preview{ sourceDir } → detected agent folders with an exists flag
POST/api/import/agents{ sourceDir, overwrite?, names? }
POST/api/import/memory/preview{ sourceDir } → detected memory items
POST/api/import/memory{ sourceDir, overwrite?, includeSecrets?, includeRuns? }

An agent folder that already exists is skipped unless overwrite: true. Secret files and run history are excluded unless you opt in, so an import cannot silently clobber the install's credentials.

Browse & entities ​

Strictly read-only. An agent's root is its agents/<name>/ directory; a project's root is its registered repo path. Every request path is resolved and guarded inside that root, symlinks included.

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/entity?kind=agent|project&name=Profile, skills, MCP servers, policy, and the memory file's relpath + existence
GET/api/browse?kind=&name=&path=Directory listing or capped text content — same 500-entry / 256 KB / 8 MB caps as the run browser

MCP ​

GET /api/entity/mcp?name= live-probes one agent's MCP servers and returns status, tools, and a needsAuth flag. POST /api/entity/mcp/auth with { name, server } begins OAuth and returns an authUrl to open; GET /api/mcp/oauth/callback is the redirect target that stores the tokens.

Realtime & voice ​

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/realtime/config{ textProvider, realtimeModel } — deliberately narrower than the full Settings snapshot
POST/api/realtime/sessionBody is the browser's SDP offer (application/sdp). Attaches PRIME's prompt and tools, authenticates upstream, and returns the SDP answer. 503 without OPENAI_API_KEY, 402 when credits block, 502 if the provider is unreachable
POST/api/voice/metrics{ turnId, committedAt, … , usage? } — the audio leg is browser↔provider, so the turn reports its own token counts, which settle into the wallet
GET/api/voice/metricsThe last 50 metrics

Telegram ​

Superadmin-only in cloud mode. The raw bot token is never returned; token changes are validated against Telegram's getMe before they are persisted and are applied to the live service without a restart.

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/telegram{ config (masked), status, accounts }
PUT/api/telegram{ enabled?, botToken?, allowedUserIds? }
POST/api/telegram/testValidate a token without saving it
POST/api/telegram/accounts/:id{ authorized } — allow or revoke one account

Onboarding ​

GET /api/onboarding returns the first-run doctor's non-secret readiness report; POST /api/onboarding/setup applies safe local auto-fixes and returns a fresh report. Superadmin-only in cloud mode.

Credits (cloud) ​

Grants and revocations live exclusively on the superadmin plane; the org plane is read-only.

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/credits{ wallet, allowance } — the balance this member may spend, after their monthly budget
GET/api/credits/usage?limit=N{ wallet, ledger, users }. Requires billing.view or usage.viewOrg. limit is clamped to 1–500, default 250

Auth ​

MethodPathBody
POST/api/auth/signup{ email, password, name }
POST/api/auth/login{ email, password }
POST/api/auth/logout—
GET/api/auth/me→ { user, orgs }
POST/api/auth/verify-email{ token }
POST/api/auth/resend-verificationSession required
POST/api/auth/forgot-password{ email } — always 200, so the endpoint cannot enumerate accounts
POST/api/auth/reset-password{ token, password }
GET/api/auth/oauth/:provider302 to the provider
GET/api/auth/oauth/:provider/callbackLogs in or links, then 302 to /
GET/api/auth/providersWhich OAuth providers are configured

Sessions ride an httpOnly saidi_session cookie with a 30-day max age. Logging out or resetting a password force-closes that user's live WebSockets.

Organizations (cloud) ​

MethodPathGate
GET/api/invites/preview?token=Public — the recipient is logged out
POST/api/orgs{ name, seats }; verified email required
GET/api/orgsYour orgs
POST/api/invites/accept{ token }
GET/api/orgOrg + seat usage
PATCH/api/org{ name?, settings? } — settings.manage
PATCH/api/org/seats{ seats } — owner
GET/api/org/membersmembers.manage
GET/api/membersThe roster every member may see

DELETE/api/org/members/:userIdmembers.manage
GET POST/api/org/invitesmembers.manage

DELETE/api/org/invites/:idmembers.manage

Changing a membership closes that member's live sockets so they re-handshake with the new governance rather than acting on cached permissions.

Admin plane (cloud) ​

Every route sits behind requireSuperadmin and operates across orgs, outside any org context.

MethodPathNotes
GET/api/admin/orgsAll orgs: seats, members, balance, burn, status
GET/api/admin/orgs/:idDrilldown: members, wallet, ledger, run counts
POST/api/admin/orgs/:id/credits{ amount, note? } — negative revokes. The only credit mutation in the product
POST/api/admin/orgs/:id/suspend · /reinstateSuspending closes every socket in the org
PATCH/api/admin/orgs/:id/limits{ maxConcurrentRuns?, seats? }
GET/api/admin/metricsPlatform totals
GET/api/admin/usersCross-org user list

Body size limits ​

JSON bodies are capped per surface: 64 KB (chat, auth, org, admin), 256 KB (cron, reflex, secret, provider, Telegram, import), 1 MB (run, memory, settings, realtime SDP), 2 MB (marketplace). Raw uploads are capped at 25 MB, webhook bodies at 1 MB, voice metrics at 32 KB.
